data.long_meaning: Originating from Old English, Leighton is derived from 'Lee' and 'Tun'. The name translates to 'light town' or 'settlement by the meadow'. The name Leighton carries the meaning “Light town” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Leighton usually hope their child will grow to embody light town and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Λείτον
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ Λείτον (Leighton) εἶναι ὄνομα τόπου ἄγιου ἤ πεδίου ἁγίου. Ἡ ἐτυμολογία αὐτοῦ προέρχεται ἀπό τὴν ἄνγλο-σαξονική λέξη 'leac' ποὺ σημαίνει 'τόπος ἄγιος' ἤ 'πεδίον ἁγίου', καὶ συνδέεται μὲ τὴν ἰδέα τῶν ἁγίων τόπων ἤ τῶν τόπων ἐκκλησιαστικῆς σημασίας.

in_english.name: Leighton
in_english.long_meaning: The name Leighton originates from the Old English words 'leac' or 'lehton', meaning 'noble town' or 'holy place'. It is derived from the combination of 'leod' (people) and 'tun' (town or settlement). Historically, Leighton has been used in England as both a surname and a given name. In Christian tradition, the name Leighton symbolizes a connection to sacred or noble places. The name carries connotations of sanctity, community, and heritage.
